title: Bracken and the Bluebell Secret
markdown:
This is a tale from the Frostcap Mountains. The mountain tops wear snow even when it is warm, and the valleys sometimes look painted a pretty blue when the day ends.

Bracken was a young ogre. Not a great stomping roaring ogre from old tales. Bracken was gentle, with eyes the colour of soft green moss after spring rain, and a smile as shy as a little deer peeking from behind a tree. His favourite time of day was when the sun dipped behind the pointy mountain tops, and the moon, like a big silver puff of a dandelion, started to float into the sky. On nights like these the world grew quiet. It felt as if the whole world held its breath, waiting for the moonbeams to paint everything in soft shimmery light.

On this particular evening the moon was as round and bright as a yummy fresh-baked cookie. It cast long dancing shadows across the soft ground. Bracken slipped out of his cosy home, which was like a big cave with piles of warm blankets made from soft wool. He was not alone. Tucked inside the pocket of his soft moss-green shirt, a pocket as deep as a comfy armchair, was a tiny kitten. Her name was Whisper. Her fur was as white and fluffy as a dandelion clock, ready to fly away in the breeze. Her eyes were like two little emeralds, always wide with wonder. Whisper wiggled with joy. She loved going on adventures in the moonlight, her tiny paws eager to explore.

“Patience now, little one.” His voice was a low rumble, like far-off thunder that promises rain, not a storm. “We are going to the bluebell wood. It is always so pretty when the moon shines on the bluebells. They sparkle like fallen stars.”

They padded softly along a twisty path. Their footsteps made barely a sound on the mossy ground. The air was cool and smelled wonderfully of pine needles, damp earth after a little shower, and the faint sweet smell of wildflowers. The Frostcap Mountains were quiet. Only the gentle whisper of the wind weaving through the old wise trees could be heard.

As they stepped into the bluebell wood, Bracken paused. His moss-green eyes looked at the familiar trees. He always loved how the moonlight peeked through the leaves, making patterns on the ground. But tonight something felt not quite right. His brow furrowed, just a little, like a tiny ripple on a calm pond. The bluebells, usually standing tall and proud, their tiny bell heads nodding happily in the breeze, seemed droopy. Their petals looked a little wilted, and their bright blue colour seemed a bit faded. It was as if they had forgotten to drink their morning dew.

“Oh dear. They look sad. It is like a really big problem has visited the bluebells.” He imagined a great smoky dragon sighing over them, its warm breath making them droop. It was a worrying thought, even for a young ogre who liked quiet walks more than big adventures.

But Whisper, always curious and always following her sharp senses, was already sniffing the air. Her tiny pink nose twitched like a butterfly’s wings. “Mew?” she seemed to ask. Her emerald eyes looked from Bracken to a faint sweet smell that was drifting on the breeze. It was a smell like warm honey mixed with ripe juicy berries. A smell that made your tummy rumble with happiness.

“What is it, Whisper?” His worry was forgotten for a moment as he followed her tiny bobbing head. She led him deeper into the woods, away from the droopy bluebells, drawn by the delightful smell that promised something yummy. Soon they came to a tiny crooked cottage nestled between two old friendly fir trees. Smoke puffed merrily from its little chimney. A warm golden light spilled from its windows. It was the home of Mr. Crumble, the goblin baker.

Mr. Crumble was a round jolly goblin. His round glasses sat right on the tip of his nose, always dusted with flour. He was carefully arranging a tray of golden-brown buns. Each one looked perfectly plump and tempting.

“Well, hello there, Bracken. And little Whisper. Lost your way? Or maybe you smelled my special blueberry buns baking?”

Bracken stepped forward. His large ogre hands clasped behind his back, a polite gesture. “Hello, Mr. Crumble. The bluebells look a bit sad tonight. I was worried a dragon might have been here.”

Mr. Crumble chuckled. It was a sound like pebbles tumbling gently in a tin. “A dragon? Oh no, my boy. The bluebells are just a little thirsty for moon-magic. And perhaps a sprinkle of something sweet.” He held up one of the buns. Its golden crust gleamed. “These are my special blueberry buns. They are baked with the brightest blueberries from the sunniest patches. I whisper good wishes into each one as I shape the dough. They are like little pockets of happiness.”

“Good wishes?” Bracken’s worry eased a little. A feeling of wonder started to grow.

“Indeed.” Mr. Crumble beamed. His eyes twinkled behind his floury spectacles. “And to help the bluebells, I have been collecting moon-dew. It is like the moon’s own gentle tears, you see. I collect it on the softest moss that grows on the north side of the oldest rocks. It gives them a little boost, a gentle nudge to stand tall.” He pointed to a small shimmering vial on his windowsill. The liquid inside seemed to hold the moonlight. “The dragon-sized problem, as you call it, is simply that the bluebells are waiting for a bit of extra sparkle, a little tender loving care. They are not scared, just a little sleepy.”

Bracken looked at the moon-dew. Its contents shimmered like captured stars. Then he looked at Whisper. She was now happily purring on Mr. Crumble’s floury apron, her tail twitching contentedly. It was not a dragon at all. Just a bit of gentle care and a baker’s thoughtful recipe. He felt a little silly for worrying so much about a dragon when all the bluebells needed was a drink.

“May we help?” His voice was hopeful. His big ogre heart filled with a desire to be useful.

“Of course.” Mr. Crumble handed Bracken the vial of moon-dew. Its glass felt cool and smooth in his large hand. He also gave him a warm blueberry bun, still radiating a gentle heat. “Share this with Whisper. She deserves a treat for leading you here. And then, carefully, sprinkle a drop or two on the bluebells. They will thank you for it with their bright blue smiles.”

With the warm bun held carefully in one hand and the shimmering vial of moon-dew in the other, Bracken and Whisper trotted back to the bluebell wood. The moonlight seemed to guide their way, painting the path ahead in silver. Bracken took a little nibble of the bun. It was warm and sweet. It tasted like sunshine and the very best kind of ripe juicy berries. Whisper nudged his hand with her tiny head. He carefully offered her a tiny piece. She gobbled it up with delight, her tiny emerald eyes sparkling with pure kitten joy.

As the moon shone brighter, casting a warm friendly glow, Bracken gently sprinkled a few drops of moon-dew onto the wilting bluebells. He watched, holding his breath. His big ogre heart beat with quiet anticipation. Slowly, as if waking from a long sleepy nap, the bluebell stems began to straighten. Their petals unfurled, delicate and soft. Their colour deepened, becoming a richer more beautiful blue, like the deepest part of the sky just before dawn. The wood seemed to glow with a soft gentle light, reflecting the moonbeams that now fell upon the revived flowers.

Bracken sat down. Whisper curled in his lap, her soft purr a gentle rhythm against his chest. He simply watched the bluebells shimmer. The air felt cosy and safe. It was filled with the scent of pine, the sweetness of blueberries from the bun, and the quiet magic of the moon. No dragon had visited. The bells stood tall again, as if they had only been waiting for a drink.
characters: Bracken (young ogre who walks in moonlight), Whisper (a white kitten with emerald eyes)
